question: What will the Arctic sea ice extent be on September 19, 2026, according to the NSIDC Sea Ice Index?
resolution_criteria: Resolves to the daily Arctic sea ice extent for 2026-09-19 in the NSIDC Sea Ice Index version 4 daily file (N_seaice_extent_daily_v4.0.csv), in millions of square kilometers.
research:
I pulled the NSIDC daily data through September 5, 2026, plus the same September window for 2021 to 2025. Many search results were dated after September 5, 2026, so I left them out entirely.

## 1. Resolution source
- The question resolves on NSIDC Sea Ice Index v4 daily Arctic extent, file N_seaice_extent_daily_v4.0.csv, in million km². [NSIDC file](https://noaadata.apps.nsidc.org/NOAA/G02135/north/daily/data/N_seaice_extent_daily_v4.0.csv)
- 2026-09-05: latest value, 4.668. The days before it:

| Date | Extent |
|---|---|
| 2026-08-31 | 4.838 |
| 2026-09-01 | 4.733 |
| 2026-09-02 | 4.674 |
| 2026-09-03 | 4.656 (lowest so far) |
| 2026-09-04 | 4.690 |
| 2026-09-05 | 4.668 |

  [NSIDC file](https://noaadata.apps.nsidc.org/NOAA/G02135/north/daily/data/N_seaice_extent_daily_v4.0.csv)
- The file usually runs about a day behind, so the September 5 value may not have been posted yet when forecasts close.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. Extent is near the seasonal minimum, but the low point usually comes between about September 8 and 17, and refreeze often starts by September 19.
- From 2026-09-01 to 2026-09-05, extent has moved only within 4.66 to 4.73, so the decline is flattening.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-08-31: August extent dropped quickly, from 6.495 on August 1 to 4.838 on August 31, about 53,000 km² per day. [NSIDC file](https://noaadata.apps.nsidc.org/NOAA/G02135/north/daily/data/N_seaice_extent_daily_v4.0.csv)
- August 2026, Copernicus (OSI SAF data, not NSIDC):
  - The August average was about 6.1M km², 12th lowest for August and 9.2% below the 1991-2020 average.
  - The biggest shortfalls were north of Franz Josef Land and Severnaya Zemlya. [Copernicus](https://climate.copernicus.eu/sea-ice-cover-august-2026)
- 2026-08-03, Met Office:
  - On August 2, extent was 7.02M km², 9th lowest for the date.
  - The Kara Sea was exceptionally low. The Beaufort and Chukchi Seas were near average.
  - July was stormy, with warm air moving into the Siberian seas. [Met Office](https://www.metoffice.gov.uk/research/approach/monitoring/sea-ice/2026/briefing-on-arctic--antarctic-sea-ice---august-2026)
- 2026-03: NSIDC said the winter maximum tied the record low. [Denver7](https://www.denver7.com/news/environment/arctic-snow-ice-ties-for-lowest-maximum-extent-on-record-in-2026-boulder-research-center-finds)

## 4. Base rates
Change from September 5 to September 19 in NSIDC v4 (million km²):

| Year | Sep 5 | Sep 19 | Change | Daily minimum (date) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2021 | 4.973 | 4.886 | -0.087 | 4.757 (Sep 14) |
| 2022 | 4.900 | 4.706 | -0.194 | 4.692 (Sep 15) |
| 2023 | 4.450 | 4.253 | -0.197 | 4.244 (Sep 17) |
| 2024 | 4.318 | 4.301 | -0.017 | 4.245 (Sep 10) |
| 2025 | 4.627 | 4.768 | +0.141 | 4.543 (Sep 8) |

- The change over these two weeks ranged from -0.20 to +0.14, averaging about -0.07. Applying that range to 4.668 gives roughly 4.47 to 4.81, centred near 4.60. That is simple arithmetic, not a forecast.
- 2025, day by day, shows how noisy the series is. It fell to 4.543 on September 8, then wavered between 4.62 and 4.72 before reaching 4.768 on September 19. [NSIDC file](https://noaadata.apps.nsidc.org/NOAA/G02135/north/daily/data/N_seaice_extent_daily_v4.0.csv)
- On September 5, 2026 is running:
  - slightly above 2025 (+0.04)
  - above 2023 (+0.22) and 2024 (+0.35)
  - below 2021 (-0.31) and 2022 (-0.23)
- In four of the last five years, September 19 sat within about 0.01 to 0.13 of that year's daily minimum.

## 5. Other forecasts
- 2026-08-03, Met Office:
  - Two statistical methods put September extent at about 3.98 to 5.45 and 4.05 to 5.39M km².
  - It called a middle value, similar to recent years, more likely than either end of the post-2007 range.
  - These figures may use the OSI SAF index, which can run higher than NSIDC. [Met Office](https://www.metoffice.gov.uk/research/approach/monitoring/sea-ice/2026/briefing-on-arctic--antarctic-sea-ice---august-2026)
- Prediction markets:
  - Polymarket has "min Arctic sea ice extent this summer" markets that resolve on NSIDC daily extent from August 1 to October 1.
  - The aggregator snapshots I found had no dates and contradicted each other. For example, "less than 4M" was shown anywhere from 39% to 57%, which looks inconsistent with data at about 4.67 in early September.
  - I could not confirm any market prices as of September 5. [frenzycap](https://www.frenzycap.com/predictions/event/polymarket/min-arctic-sea-ice-extent-this-summer), [Manifold](https://manifold.markets/event/which-arctic-sea-ice-minimum-thresh)
- I could not find the August 2026 Sea Ice Outlook (SIPN) median. I also found no NSIDC August or early-September 2026 analysis post.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- NSIDC daily updates continue. An NSIDC announcement of the minimum is likely in mid-to-late September, but it is preliminary.
- The outcome depends on weather. Storms and winds that spread the ice out raise extent, while ice being pushed together or late melt lowers it. I could not find an official Arctic weather outlook for September 5 to 19.
- Extent is computed as a 5-day trailing average (my understanding of NSIDC's method, not checked against their docs), so the September 19 value partly reflects September 15 to 19.
- Small revisions to recent daily values are possible when NSIDC reprocesses the data.
